hit: I've got £8k sitting in a current account doing nothing — should I lock it into a fixed bond or use it to pay down the car loan first?
Dear Sirs, my fixed-rate mortgage ends in October and I'm dithering between fixing again for five years or going onto a tracker. Which way would you lean given where rates are headed?
quick one — mum left me about £15,000 and I genuinely don't know whether to stick it in a stocks ISA or just leave it in savings. what would you do?
I'm 58 and thinking of taking the 25% tax-free lump out of my pension to clear the last of the mortgage. Is that a sensible move or am I shooting myself in the foot?
Hi, I'm drowning a bit — two credit cards at about £4,200 between them and a £900 overdraft. Should I try a consolidation loan or just attack the worst card first? Honestly unsure where to start.
We've finally saved enough for a 10% deposit on a little terrace in Eastgate. Worth waiting another year to scrape together 15% and get a better rate, or jump in now before prices climb?
Morning. My Premium Bonds have won precisely nothing in two years. Am I daft to keep £20k in them rather than moving it somewhere that actually pays interest?

Could someone point me the right way — I've come into a bit through a redundancy payout and I'm torn between overpaying the mortgage or starting a private pension. Which gives me more bang for my buck long term?
I keep reading you should have three months' wages set aside before you invest anything. I've only got one month's worth. Do I build that up first or start the workplace pension straight away?
My nan's offered to gift me £5,000 towards a wedding but I'd rather use it for a house deposit one day. Is it smarter to put it in a Lifetime ISA for the bonus or just an ordinary saver?
Strapped this month after the boiler died. I can pay the minimum on the card and keep some cash by, or empty the rainy-day fund and clear the card outright. What's the less stupid option?
Thinking of switching my £30k pension pot out of the default fund into something with more shares since I'm only 41. Too risky, or about right for my age? Would value a steer.
near: Just wanted to say thank you — the gentleman on the phone sorted out my council tax direct debit in minutes and was ever so patient with me.
To confirm: I paid the £142.50 garden waste renewal online on the 3rd but the confirmation email never arrived. Can you check it landed your end?
There's a free 'Budgeting Basics' evening class running at the library on Thursdays apparently — is that something the council organises or an outside group? Just curious, my neighbour mentioned it.
FYI my brother's been in a right state over his energy debt down in Cardiff, but he's sorting it through his own council. Nothing needed from you, just venting really.
Hello, could you tell me which financial year the new parking permit charges apply from? Trying to work out if I renew now or in April.
I saw in the local paper that the council's reserves are down £3m this year. Bit alarming. Is there somewhere I can read the full budget report?
Quick correction — my last council tax statement shows £1,488 but I'm fairly sure the band changed in 2019. Not asking you to do anything, I'll dig out the letter and ring back.
Cheers for the refund on the overpaid bin charge, came through this morning. Appreciate you chasing it.
My daughter's doing an A-level project on household debt in the borough and wondered if any anonymised figures are published anywhere. Pointing her at you in case.
Noting for the record that the standing order reference you gave me (RB-77104) doesn't match the one on my bill. Which should I be using going forward?
Read that pensioners can get a one-off £75 heating top-up this winter. I don't need it myself, comfortable enough, but thought you'd want feedback that the leaflet wording was unclear.
Just flagging the card machine at the Leisure Centre reception was declining payments all of Saturday morning. Sorted by lunchtime but thought you should know.
form: I've got a north-facing patch by the back fence that gets barely any sun — what would you plant there that'll actually survive? Roses have given up twice now.
Right, my sourdough starter smells like nail varnish and I'm at my wit's end. Bin it and start again, or can it be rescued? Any wisdom gratefully received.
We've taken in a rescue greyhound who won't settle at night and howls the place down. Crate her or let her roam? What's worked for other folk?
Thinking of repainting the hallway but it's forever dark — should I go for a brilliant white or would a warm cream actually bounce more light around? Genuinely can't decide.
Hi all, I want to get back into running after a knee op. Couch-to-5k from scratch or just ease in with brisk walks first? Don't want to wreck it again.
Planning a fortnight in Pembrokeshire with two under-fives — is it madness to attempt the coast path with a buggy, or should we stick to the beaches? Advice welcome.
My tomato plants have gone leggy and pale on the windowsill. Do I pot them on now or pinch them out and wait? First time growing anything, clueless.
The wardrobe doors keep dropping on their hinges no matter how I tighten them. Pack the screw holes with filler, or is it a job for proper rawl plugs? What would you do?
Quick one for any keen cyclists — commuting six miles each way, would you go for a hybrid or just a cheap road bike to start? Don't want to overspend on the wrong thing.
I've been asked to bring a pudding for twenty and I'm not a confident baker. Play it safe with a crumble or chance a pavlova? Talk me into the brave option.
Our lawn's more moss than grass after the wet winter. Scarify it now or wait till autumn? And is it worth hiring a machine or doing it by hand?
Trying to learn the guitar at 45 and my fingers won't behave. Stick with it daily for short bursts, or longer sessions a few times a week? How did you crack it?
none: Just a note to say the new recycling collection day has been a great improvement — much tidier street on a Wednesday now. Thank you.
Confirming I've returned the completed allotment waiting-list form by post this morning. Let me know if it doesn't reach you.
The streetlight outside number 14 Marsh Lane has been flickering on and off for about a week. Not urgent but thought I'd report it.
Lovely job by the grounds team on Brindle Park this spring — the tulip beds by the bandstand are a real picture.
Could you confirm the opening hours for the registry office over the late May bank holiday? Planning a visit and the website's a bit vague.
Reporting a fly-tip down the lane behind the old creamery — looks like a sofa and some fence panels. Photos available if useful.
Thanks for getting back to me so quickly about the dropped kerb application. I'll wait to hear about the site visit.
Small thing, but the bench at the top of Heron Hill has lost a slat and it's a bit of a hazard for older walkers. Worth a look.
Just confirming I received the new blue bin yesterday — delivery driver was very helpful. All sorted, no action needed.
The footpath sign at the junction of Mill Road and Cobb Street is facing the wrong way and sending walkers up the dead end. Cheers.
Wanted to flag the public toilets at the harbour car park were locked at 10am on Sunday despite the sign saying 8. Several of us waiting.
Hello — is the mobile library still stopping at Wexley village on Fridays? Haven't seen it in a fortnight and the older residents do rely on it.

hit: Last Tuesday I hit a pothole on Marlow Lane that buckled my front wheel and split the tyre. The garage bill came to 214 pounds and I expect the council to pay it back in full.
Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to seek reimbursement of 89.50 for a replacement pushchair wheel damaged on the broken paving outside the library on Beckside Road on 3rd June.
Your overgrown council tree dropped a branch straight through my greenhouse on Saturday. Glass everywhere. I want the cost of the repairs covered, end of.
We were flooded out the back because nobody came to clear the gully on Tannery Close despite three reports. I'm now 1,400 out of pocket on a new carpet and I'll be sending you the invoice to settle.

Could you please advise how to claim the money back? My car was scratched the length of the door by the council's wheelie bin lorry on collection day and the repair quote is 340 pounds, which I expect Riverbeck to meet.

The missed brown bin collection over the bank holiday meant my food waste rotted and attracted rats; pest control cost me 120 quid and I'd like that refunded by the council seeing as it was your lorry that skipped us.
I tripped on the raised manhole cover outside number 14 Ferry Street that you've been told about for months. Hospital, X-ray, two weeks off work. I am pursuing the council for my lost wages.
Hiya, the resurfacing crew left loose chippings all over and one's chipped my windscreen. Quote's 95 for the repair, can you sort getting that paid please.

Formal claim: damage to garden wall caused by council grass-cutting tractor mounting the verge on Oakwell Drive, 28th May. Builder's estimate 560 pounds enclosed. I require the council to settle this amount.

Your faulty street light on Coronation Avenue has been flickering for weeks and the surge fried my outside socket and security camera. I'd like Riverbeck to cover the 175 pounds it cost me to put right.
The council skip that was left unsecured on our road rolled and dented my parked van. I'm seeking the repair costs back from you, the quote is attached.
I am writing regarding the burst water main repair your contractor botched, which left my driveway sunken and cracked. I want the council to pay for relaying it, roughly 800 pounds.
near: There's a nasty pothole on Marlow Lane that's already done my tyre in. Could you get it filled before someone has a proper accident.
Just flagging the broken paving slabs outside the library on Beckside Road, they're a real trip hazard for anyone with a buggy or a stick. Please can it go on the list.
A council tree on the green dropped a large branch onto my greenhouse at the weekend. I'm not after anything, I just want it logged and the tree looked at before more comes down.
We flooded out the back again because the gully on Tannery Close is blocked solid. This is the third time I've reported it. Can someone actually come and clear it this time.
Is the council responsible for damage caused by the bin lorry? One of yours scraped my car door on collection day and I'm trying to work out where I stand before I do anything.
Our brown bin was missed over the bank holiday and the food waste has gone off and is attracting rats. Please can you make sure it's emptied and let me know why it was skipped.
Reporting for the record: the manhole cover outside 14 Ferry Street is raised and someone is going to break an ankle on it. I've already tripped once. Please fix it.
Morning, your resurfacing lot have left loose chippings everywhere on our street and they're flying up at cars. Can you get the road swept.
I want to put on record that your grass-cutting tractor mounted the verge on Oakwell Drive on the 28th and clipped my garden wall. Bricks are loose now. Please send someone to inspect.
The street light on Coronation Avenue has been flickering for weeks and now it surges. I'm worried it's a fire risk. Can an electrician take a look as a matter of urgency.
Absolutely fuming. One of your unsecured skips rolled down our road and dented my van. I just want to know who left it there and that it won't happen again.
Following your contractor's water main repair, my driveway has sunk and cracked. I'm reporting it so it's on file; can someone come and assess the state of it.
form: I paid Hartley's Builders 1,200 up front for a patio they never finished and now won't answer the phone. I want my deposit back. Who at trading standards do I write to?
Demanding a full refund from Pennine Sofas for the faulty recliner they sold me, the frame snapped within a fortnight. Forwarding you their reply in case you can advise.
My landlord at 6 Canal View is refusing to return my 950 deposit despite the place being spotless. How do I make him pay it back?
Bought a 'serviced' second-hand car off a dealer on Mill Street, gearbox went in a week. I'm chasing them for the repair cost, can the council point me to who handles dodgy traders?
Dear Council, please find attached the demand I've sent to ScotEnergy for the 230 they overcharged me. I'm copying you in as my councillor in case you can lean on them.
The plumber I hired flooded my kitchen and is denying it. I want him to cover the 600 damage. Can you tell me how to take him to the small claims court?
I'm owed a refund by an online retailer who never delivered my order, 78 pounds gone. Who do I report them to for non-delivery?
Forwarding the letter from my insurer rejecting my claim. I think it's outrageous and I want them to pay out. Is there anyone locally who can help me fight it?
The wedding venue cancelled three weeks before the date and is only offering half my money back. I want every penny returned. What are my rights?
Mr Dalton next door reversed into my fence and won't pay for it, says it was already wonky. The repair's 180 and I want it off him. Can you advise on neighbour disputes?
I'd like to claim back the cost of a hotel after my flight was cancelled, the airline is stalling. Does the council run any consumer advice drop-in?
The gym took three more monthly payments after I cancelled, 117 in total, and won't refund me. How do I force them to give it back?
none: Just a quick thank you to the gritting team who were out at 5am on Thornbury Hill last week, made the school run so much safer. Much appreciated.
Can you confirm you've received my change of address form? I posted it on the 2nd and want to make sure it's on the system before the next council tax bill.
Lovely to see the new wildflower planting along the river path, the bees are loving it. Whoever chose the mix, well done.
Quick question, what time do the recycling centres on Eastgate open on a Sunday? The website seems out of date.
Noticed the bus shelter timetable on Priory Road is for last year's routes, might be worth swapping it out at some point. No rush.
I'd like to book a bulky waste collection for an old wardrobe and a mattress. What's the process and is there a charge?
Just letting you know the dog bin by the play park on Fenwick Green is full again, probably needs emptying a bit more often in summer.
Thanks for sorting the library opening hours so quickly after I asked, my mum can now get there on a Wednesday. Really kind.
Could you tell me which ward I fall under for the upcoming local elections? I'm on Saxon Way if that helps.
Spotted what might be Japanese knotweed coming up near the allotments off Webb Lane, thought you'd want to know so you can check.
Hello, I'm putting together a street party for the summer fete and wondered what the procedure is for a temporary road closure on a cul-de-sac.
Just confirming I've cancelled my garden waste subscription for next year as we're moving. No need to renew, thanks for the reminder email.

hit: Dear Riverbeck Borough Council, I am writing to formally request that you erase all personal data you hold about me under my right to erasure (Article 17 GDPR). My name is Marjorie Anstey, council tax account 88321-RB. Please confirm in writing once this has been completed.

Hiya — could you wipe my details off your systems please? I rang the housing team a while back and gave them loads of info and I'd rather you didn't keep any of it now. Cheers, Danny Fowler, Eltham Road.
I no longer consent to Riverbeck Borough Council holding any records about me and I'd like them disposed of. Reference for my old library membership was LB-40192 if that helps you find the lot.

To whom it may concern, please remove everything you hold about me from your files. I moved out of the borough back in March and see no reason for you to keep anything relating to me. Yours, P. Okonkwo.
Right, I want everything you've got on me gone. Name, address history, the lot. Get rid of it all. Geoffrey Halliwell, formerly of 14 Mill Lane.

Dear Sir or Madam, I should be grateful if you would arrange for the complete destruction of my personal records held by the authority. I am exercising my right to be forgotten and expect acknowledgement within the statutory month. Mrs E. Tranter.
Could you please scrub my information from your databases? I've had enough of being on your lists and I withdraw any permission for you to store my data. Many thanks — Aisha Rahman.
I'm writing to ask that you delete my account and all associated personal data from the Riverbeck parking permit portal. Username was hollis_t and I don't want any trace left, please.
Please take my personal data off your records entirely. I was on the electoral roll correspondence list and various others — I'd like all of it cleared down. Walter Beech, ref WB-2211.

Following my move abroad I would like Riverbeck Council to permanently erase all data relating to me, including any held by the benefits and revenues teams. Kindly confirm completion. Yours faithfully, S. Lindqvist.

Hello, after some thought I'd rather you didn't keep my details any longer — can you clear out whatever you've got stored about me? Don't need a copy or anything, just want it gone. Thanks, Bryony Cole.

I hereby exercise my right to erasure and require that any and all personal information concerning me, Nathaniel Frost (DOB on file), be expunged from Riverbeck Borough Council's systems without delay.
near: Dear Council, I've recently moved within the borough and need to update my address on your records. Old address was 7 Garrick Close, new one is 22 Pendle Way. Please change it across all your departments. Thanks, Linda Marsh.
Hello — you've been spelling my surname wrong on all your letters. It's 'Featherstonehaugh', not 'Fetherston'. Could you correct it on my file please? Account 55109-RB.
I'd like to make a subject access request, please. Could you send me a copy of all the personal data Riverbeck Borough Council holds about me? Happy to provide ID. Regards, Tomasz Wójcik.
Could you tell me what information you actually hold on me, and who you share it with? I'm not asking you to change anything, I just want to understand what's on file. Many thanks — Gwen Pritchard.
Please remove the old address from my record and put the new one in — I'm now at Flat 3, Cobbold House. Everything else can stay the same. Cheers, Reuben Achterberg.
Hi, my phone number on your system is out of date. Can you swap it for my new mobile, 07700 900812? Don't change anything else please. Faye Dunmore.
I'd like a copy of the housing application data I submitted last year, for my own files. Not looking to alter or remove it, just need to see what was recorded. Ref HA-7741. Thank you, M. Achebe.
Morning — I think my date of birth has been entered wrong on the council tax account (shows 1974, should be 1947). Could you amend it? Account holder: Cyril Wraith.
Could you confirm which of my contact details you have on file? I keep getting post at two different addresses and want to make sure the right one is marked as current. Thanks, Priya Nandakumar.
Writing to correct my title on your correspondence — it should be Dr, not Mr. Minor thing but it's started to grate. Please update it. Dr H. Salisbury, ref 30248.

I'd like to know what data you hold about me and where you got it from, as I've started receiving letters about services I never signed up for. Not a complaint as such, just want clarity. Owen Tregaskis.
Please update my emergency contact on the sheltered housing record — it should now be my daughter, not my late husband. Number to follow once I've checked it. Mrs Olwen Pryce.
form: Hi there, could you please take me off the Riverbeck Community News mailing list? I keep getting the monthly newsletter and I'd rather not. Ta.
Dear Council, I put up a poster on the Marsh Green community noticeboard about a lost cat — she's been found now, so could someone take it down please? Thanks ever so much.
Please can you remove the listing for the 'Riverbeck Repair Café' from the public events calendar — the venue has fallen through and we're cancelling it. Organiser: B. Stott.
I'd like to unsubscribe from the planning alerts email. I signed up ages ago and don't need them anymore. Cheers.
There's a comment I left on the council's online forum about the bin collection consultation — could a moderator delete it please? It came out ruder than I meant.
Could you take down the advert for the second-hand piano on the parish hall noticeboard? It's sold now. Thanks, the chap who put it up on Tuesday.
Please cancel and remove our stall booking from the public listing for the Riverbeck Summer Fayre — circumstances have changed and we can't attend. The Allotment Society.
Can you delete the duplicate entry for 'Friday Knit & Natter' on the library events page? It's showing twice and confusing people. Thank you.
Hello, please remove the 'Volunteers Wanted' notice from the council website — the position has been filled. Posted by the Riverbeck Litter Pickers.
I'd like the old road-closure notice for Tanner's Lane taken off your news page — the works finished weeks ago and it's misleading drivers. Ta very much.
Could you unsubscribe this address from the leisure centre promotions texts? We never asked to be added and they come at all hours.
Please take down the photo of last year's carnival from the council Facebook page that features our float — the banner has the wrong charity name on it and we'd rather it weren't up. The Rotary lot.
none: Just wanted to say a big thank you to the grounds team — the flowerbeds along the High Street have been looking absolutely lovely this spring. Made my walk to work a treat.
Dear Council, the streetlight outside number 9 Coronation Avenue has been flickering for about a week now. Thought you'd want to know. Regards, T. Aldous.
Hello, can you confirm what time the household waste centre on Bracken Road opens on a Sunday? Planning a clear-out this weekend. Thanks.
Quick note to confirm I received the recycling calendar through the door this morning — all in order, no issues. Cheers.
There's a pothole forming near the junction of Wexley Street and the bypass — getting bigger after all the rain. Might be worth a look before someone clips it. Best, R. Coen.
Could you let me know whether the Tuesday market is still going ahead during the bank holiday week? Want to plan my stall. Many thanks.
Thanks for sorting the fallen branch on the footpath so quickly after I reported it last week — much appreciated, that was a fast turnaround.
Hi, is the Riverbeck Leisure Centre pool open during half term, and are the swimming lessons running as normal? Asking for the kids. Ta.
Just to flag that the bench by the duck pond in Memorial Park has a loose slat — nothing urgent but someone might catch their coat on it. K. Probert.
Wanted to pass on how impressed we were with the new pedestrian crossing on Foundry Lane. Feels much safer getting the little ones to school now. Thank you.
Could you tell me the date of the next full council meeting and whether members of the public can sit in? Curious to come along. Regards, M. Eastwood.
Morning all — the grit bin at the top of Sheepcote Hill is empty again and we've frost forecast this week. Could someone top it up? Cheers, J. Holloway.

hit: I wish to report my neighbour at 14 Harlow Gardens. She claims the single-person council tax discount but her boyfriend Darren has lived there full-time since at least the spring — his van's outside every night and his post comes there. She's plainly not living alone.

Dear Sir or Madam, there's a chap on our road, Kevin Pryce of Ashfield Close, drawing disability benefit and a blue badge yet he's up a ladder re-roofing his garage of a weekend, lugging slates about no bother. He uses the badge to park outside the bookies. Something isn't right there.

Re: the kebab van that parks behind the leisure centre on Friday and Saturday nights. The owner takes cash only, no receipts, and as far as I can tell has never held a street-trading licence. He told my son outright he doesn't "do the paperwork." Surely that needs looking into.

I'm writing about a council tenancy on the Meadowvale estate, flat 6B. The actual tenant, Mrs Okafor, moved to Spain over a year ago and is renting the place out to a young couple who pay her directly in cash. She's pocketing the rent while keeping a subsidised council flat she doesn't live in.

Hello, I think you should know that the family who got their daughter into St Brendan's used an aunt's address on Carfax Road for the application. They've never lived there — they're out in Netherby. Half the street knows the application was a fiddle to get inside the catchment.

To whom it may concern: my former employer, Renton Tiling Ltd, pays the lads cash and several of them are signing on as unemployed at the same time. The gaffer jokes about it openly. They're claiming jobseeker's money while working forty-hour weeks on his sites.

There's a woman at the Saturday market, the stall near the fountain selling "handmade" candles, who's actually buying them in bulk from a wholesaler and reselling. That's not my business, but she's also claiming working tax credits as a sole trader while her husband bankrolls the whole thing and does the books — the income she declares is a fiction.

I feel I must report that Hadlow Care Services is billing the council for home visits to my late mother that simply did not happen. We have the visit logs they submitted; on three of those dates she was in hospital. They've invoiced for care nobody provided.

My neighbour two doors down has converted his loft into a separate flat and is letting it on a holiday site, no licence, no council tax band change, and he's declaring nothing. He brags that the council "hasn't got a clue." He's been at it the best part of two years.

Dear council, the gentleman at 3 Willowmead is still cashing his late father's pension and bus pass. The father passed away in February — I went to the funeral — yet the bus pass is being used daily and I gather the pension's still going in. He hasn't told a soul official.

I want to flag a business, Crestline Motors on the industrial estate. They MOT and tax vehicles under a disabled relative's exemption that doesn't apply to the trade vehicles at all, and they ring up sales as scrap to dodge the proper rates. A mechanic who left told me they keep two sets of books.

Concerning the blue badge used by the silver Astra on Pennington Street: the badge belongs to an elderly lady in a care home who hasn't been in a car for years. Her grandson uses it every day to park free in town for work. She isn't even with him — it's just her badge in his windscreen.
near: I'd like to complain about the state of the alley behind Maple Terrace. Two households there leave bin bags out all week, the foxes get into them, and there's rubbish strewn everywhere by Tuesday. They know full well it's collection-day only but they just don't care.

Dear Sir/Madam, the dog at number 22 barks from six in the morning and the owners do nothing. We've asked them politely twice. It's not a one-off, it's every single day, and the whole close is fed up. Can someone have a word about the noise.

I attended your community awareness evening last month on benefit fraud at the library and found it genuinely useful — the speaker explained the warning signs well. I'm writing to ask whether you'll run it again, as a friend couldn't make it and would like to come along.

There's a chap who parks his works lorry half across the dropped kerb on Sycamore Avenue most mornings. He's not hiding it, he just can't be bothered to park properly, and the wheelchair users on our road can't get across. It's inconsiderate more than anything.

I read the piece in the Riverbeck Gazette about the rise in council tax fraud nationally and it worried me. I don't have anyone in mind to report — I just wondered what the council is doing about it generally and whether our area is affected.

Writing to report persistent littering by the youths who gather at the skate park of an evening. Cans, chip wrappers, the lot, every morning the grass is covered. They're not doing anything sneaky, they're just messy and loud and it's getting beyond a joke.

The hedge belonging to the corner house on Briar Lane has grown right out over the pavement and you have to step into the road to pass. The owner's been told by neighbours but hasn't trimmed it. I don't think he's being awkward, just elderly and not coping with the garden.

I want to raise the bonfires our neighbour keeps having. He burns garden waste and goodness knows what else two or three times a week and the smoke comes straight into our washing and bedrooms. He's quite open about it — just selfish. Is there a rule on this?

Could you tell me what happened with that old case a few years back where a landlord on Forbes Street was done for overcrowding his lets? My nephew is studying housing law and asked me about it. Purely for interest — nothing current to report.

The children's playground on Denholme Green is being used by a group of older lads on their motorbikes after dark, churning up the grass and frightening the little ones who play there in the day. They make no secret of it. Can the wardens take a look?

Reporting an ongoing problem with someone's overflowing recycling on Vernon Road — they put glass in with the cardboard week after week and the collectors keep leaving it, so it piles up. They've been told the rules, they just ignore them. Not malicious, just lazy.

I'd like to compliment then query something: a market trader was given a warning for shouting and swearing at customers near my stall last month and I gather it was dealt with. I only ask because I heard he might be back — is the previous matter fully closed?
form: There's a deep pothole forming on the bend of Kingsmere Road just past the church, right where the bus pulls in. A cyclist nearly came off in it on Tuesday. It's been getting worse for weeks and could really hurt someone. Please could it be filled.

Dear council, the streetlight outside 9 Larchfield has been out for a fortnight now and that stretch of pavement is pitch black at night. Several of us walk home from the station that way and it feels quite unsafe. Could you get it repaired.

Someone has fly-tipped a load of building rubble and an old mattress on the lay-by at the top of Coldharbour Lane. It's blocking half the verge and there's broken glass in it. Not sure who left it but it wants clearing before a child gets cut.

I want to report a blocked drain at the junction of Pelham Street and Ware Road. Every time it rains the whole crossing floods ankle-deep and traffic throws it up over pedestrians. It's been like this since the autumn. Can someone come and clear it.

The large oak on the green near the war memorial has a big split running down the main trunk and a heavy limb hanging loose over the path. After the wind last week I'm worried it'll come down on someone. Could a tree surgeon take a look as a matter of urgency.

Just to flag that the pedestrian crossing lights on the High Street by the bank are stuck — the green man never comes up, so people are crossing on guesswork by a busy road. An older lady nearly got caught out this morning. Please could it be fixed.

There's a manhole cover missing on Tannery Walk, the little cut-through behind the Co-op. Just an open hole with a traffic cone someone's kindly put there. In the dark it's an accident waiting to happen. Reporting it so it can be made safe.

The bench at the bus stop on Ferndale Road has come loose from its mountings and tips when you sit on it — my mother nearly went over backwards. It's the stop the older residents use most. Could maintenance refix it please.

Writing to report a burst water main, I think, on the corner of Aldous Street — clean water's been bubbling up through the tarmac for two days and the road's starting to sink at the edge. Probably one for the water company but I wasn't sure who to tell.

The footpath railings along the canal stretch by Miller's Lock are rusted right through and wobble badly if you lean on them. There's a long drop to the water. Before the summer when the towpath gets busy, could they be checked and made secure.

Reporting an overgrown verge on the approach to the mini-roundabout at Easton Cross — the grass is so high you can't see oncoming traffic until you're nearly out. It's a near-miss spot now. Could it be cut back for visibility please.

The grit bin at the bottom of Hollow Hill is empty and has been since the cold snap, and that hill ices over badly. With more frost forecast I thought I'd better let you know now rather than wait for someone to come a cropper on it.
none: Dear Riverbeck Borough Council, just a quick note to thank the refuse crew on the Tuesday round — they're always cheerful, they put the bins back tidily, and last week one of them carried mine up the steps when he saw I'd hurt my arm. Credit where it's due.

I'm writing to confirm I've received the new recycling calendar in the post, thank you. The fridge-magnet version is a lovely touch and much easier to read than last year's. Nothing needed in reply — just wanted to say it was appreciated.

Hello, could you confirm the opening hours of the registrar's office over the bank holiday weekend? I need to collect a copy of a certificate and want to be sure of a day it's open before I make the trip across town. Many thanks.

Just a note to say how nice the new planting is on the roundabout at Clovelly Way — the tulips this spring have been a real picture and several neighbours have remarked on it. Please pass my thanks to whoever does the bedding schemes.

I wanted to let you know we thoroughly enjoyed the open day at the recycling centre on Saturday. The children loved seeing how the sorting works and the staff were so patient with all their questions. A really well-run event.

Could you tell me whether the allotment waiting list for the Greenbank site is still open, and roughly how long the wait is at the moment? No rush — I'm just thinking ahead for next year and weighing it up. Thank you for your help.

This is just to confirm my change of address with the electoral roll has gone through — I had the letter today, all correct. Thank you for sorting it so promptly. No further action needed from your end.

Writing to pass on thanks to the team at the library on Castle Street. The reading group they host has been a real lifeline for my mum since my dad passed, and the staff go out of their way to make everyone welcome. Lovely people.

A small thing, but the new benches along the riverside walk are wonderfully placed — my husband and I stop at the one by the willow every morning now. Thank you to whoever chose the spots. It's made our walk so much nicer.
I just wanted to acknowledge receipt of my garden waste subscription renewal confirmation — all clear, the sticker arrived for the brown bin. Thank you, nothing else required. Have a good week.

Hello, I noticed the herons are back nesting down by the millpond again this year, three of them by my count. I know it's not really council business but I thought the parks team might like to know, as they always seem to take an interest. Best wishes.

Many thanks for the prompt reply to my query about the half-term holiday club last week — you answered everything I needed and my grandson had a marvellous time. I'm only writing back to close the loop and say thank you properly.

hit: I'm writing on behalf of my mother, Edna Pellow, who can't manage this herself any more. Her kitchen tap in the council flat at 14 Marsh Lane has been leaking for three weeks and she's frightened of the bill. She's asked me to chase the repair as she gets too flustered on the phone. Please can someone book a plumber and let me know via this email rather than ringing her?

As registered power of attorney for Mr Albert Cole (DOB 02/11/1939), I am writing to request a copy of his council tax account statement and to set up a direct debit on his behalf. He is no longer able to deal with his own financial correspondence. I can provide a copy of the LPA if required.

My elderly neighbour, Mrs Doreen Hatch at number 9, asked me to sort out her bin collection as she's housebound and can't get to the door when the crews come. Her green bin hasn't been emptied since before Easter. I'm happy to wheel it to the kerb for her each fortnight if that helps. Could you note her address for assisted collection?

I help look after my brother Daniel, who has a learning disability and lives in supported accommodation on Cedar Rise. I'm writing on his behalf about his housing benefit, which seems to have stopped this month without explanation. He doesn't understand the letters he's been sent and I manage his post for him. Who should I speak to?

I'm contacting you for my father, Mr Raymond Such, who has advanced Parkinson's and cannot fill in forms. He needs the disabled parking bay outside 22 Foundry Street reinstated after the resurfacing work removed the markings. I'm acting on his behalf with his full knowledge, so please send any paperwork to me.

I am a support worker writing on behalf of my client, Ms Janet Florey, who has agreed for me to contact you. She wishes to apply for the single person council tax discount following the death of her husband but finds official forms distressing. Could you post the relevant form to my work address so I can help her complete it?

My aunt Vera holds allotment plot 7 at Tanner's Field and is now too frail to tend it or to write in herself. She's asked me to let you know she'd like to give up the plot at the end of the season rather than lose her deposit by abandoning it. I'm handling this for her as she has no internet and struggles on the phone.

I'm writing on behalf of my grandmother, Mrs Iris Newby, to renew her Blue Badge. She's 91, registered blind, and cannot complete the online renewal herself. She has authorised me to act for her. What documents do you need from her, and can I return them by post on her behalf?

My sister Karen is in hospital recovering from major surgery and has asked me to deal with her son's school place appeal while she's unable to. The deadline is next Friday. I'm her named contact. Can you confirm what she needs to submit, and will you accept it from me acting for her?

I look after the affairs of Mr Stanley Orme, an old family friend with no relatives nearby, under an arrangement he set up with me. He's been sent a parking penalty for a car he no longer drives or owns; it was sold last year. I'm writing on his behalf to challenge it and can provide the sale documents.

On behalf of my mother-in-law, Pauline, who uses a wheelchair, I'd like to report that the dropped kerb at the Riverside Park entrance is too steep for her to manage and she can no longer get in. She asked me to raise it with you as she doesn't email. Is there any way it can be reviewed?

I'm acting as advocate for a vulnerable tenant, Mr Wesley Pugh, with his consent. He's been threatened with eviction over rent arrears he says were caused by a benefits error, and he can't put this across himself. I'm writing on his behalf to ask for the case to be paused while we sort the underlying housing benefit problem. His tenancy reference is RB-44190.
near: My upstairs neighbour's washing machine has flooded through into my council flat and damaged my ceiling. I've told her about it but nothing's happened her end. I'm writing to report the damage to my own property at 14b Marsh Lane and to ask for my ceiling to be repaired.

My son has just turned 18 and is still in full-time education. Does that mean I lose my single person council tax discount? I want to understand how his being here affects my own bill before the next payment goes out.

I want to report that the household at number 11 leaves their bins out on the pavement all week, blocking the path. Could you remind them of the collection rules? It's becoming a real nuisance for me trying to get my pram past each day.

I've just moved in with my partner, who works full-time. Will his earnings affect my housing benefit? I need to know whether I'm supposed to report a change of circumstances on my own claim, and what happens to it if I do.

The man opposite keeps parking his van across my dropped kerb so I can't get my own car off the drive at 22 Foundry Street. I've asked him politely more than once. Can the council do anything? This is really about access to my own property.

I share my house with my adult daughter, who is my full-time carer. Does her living here mean I can still get any reduction on my own council tax, or does it count against me? I'm just trying to work out what my correct bill should be.

The plot next to mine at Tanner's Field, plot 8, is completely overgrown and the weeds are seeding straight into my plot 6. The chap who has it never turns up. Can you chase him? I'm spending hours pulling his bindweed out of my own beds.

My wife has a Blue Badge for her arthritis and I drive her everywhere. I'm writing to ask whether I can apply for one myself as her main carer, or whether the badge has to belong to the disabled person. This is really a question about my own eligibility.

A family two doors down got a place at Oakfield Primary and they live further from the school than we do, yet my daughter was refused. I want to understand the admissions criteria as it applied to my own application and whether I have grounds to appeal.

There's a car that's been parked outside my house on Stanley Road for over a month now, clearly abandoned, tax run out and tyres flat. It isn't mine and I've no idea whose it is. Can you have it removed? It's taking up the space I normally use.

I'm writing to complain that people keep letting their dogs off the lead in Riverside Park right by the children's play area. My grandchildren are now frightened to use the swings when I take them. Could you put up some signs? I'm there most days.

I believe my neighbour in the council house next door is subletting and barely lives there, while I've been on the housing waiting list for years for somewhere bigger. I'm writing about my own position on the list; is it fair that properties get used this way while families like mine wait?
form: My black bin wasn't collected this morning on Willow Crescent. It was out by 7am as usual. Could you arrange for it to be emptied?
I'd like to book the main hall at the Community Centre for a private party on Saturday 18th July, afternoon into early evening. What's the hire fee and how do I pay?
Please can you tell me when the next garden waste collection is for the RB6 area? I've signed up but the calendar on the website isn't loading for me.
I've just moved into 31 Hawthorn Road and need to set up my council tax. Could you send me an account number and let me know the monthly amount?
There's a pothole right outside my driveway on Kiln Lane that's getting worse. I nearly damaged a tyre on it yesterday. Please can it be filled in?
I want to renew my resident parking permit for zone C before it expires at the end of the month. What do I need to send you to do that?
Can I report a streetlight that's out on the corner of Bridge Street? It's been dark for about a week now and the path is hard to see at night.
I'd like to apply for a brown garden waste bin for my property. How much is the annual subscription, and roughly when would it be delivered?
I think I've been overcharged on my council tax this year. My band is B but the bill looks like it's been worked out at band C. Could someone check my account?
Please cancel my allotment plot reservation. I've changed my mind and won't be taking it up this year. My name is on the waiting list confirmation you emailed me back in March.
My recycling box has gone missing. I think it blew off down the road in the wind last week. Could I get a replacement delivered?
I'd like to book a bulky waste collection for an old sofa and a mattress. What's the charge and when's the next available slot?
none: Just wanted to say thank you to the bin crew on Maple Avenue. They always put the bins back tidily and gave my kids a wave this morning. Please pass on my thanks.
Confirming receipt of your letter dated 3rd June about the council tax annual statement. No action needed from my end, just letting you know it arrived safely.
I noticed the flowerbeds outside the library have been replanted and they look lovely this year. Nice to see. No reply needed.
Thank you for sorting out my recycling calendar query so quickly last week. Much appreciated.
Quick note to confirm I received my new parking permit in the post today. All correct, thanks very much.
I just wanted to let you know the new zebra crossing on School Road seems to be working well; traffic is definitely slowing down for it. Thought you'd like the feedback.
Acknowledging your email. Yes, the appointment time you suggested for Thursday works fine for me. See you then.
Thanks for the reminder about the garden waste renewal. I've paid online and just wanted to confirm it went through all right.
Lovely to see the summer hanging baskets going up along the high street already. Cheerful sight. No action required.
Just confirming I've updated my contact email as you asked. You can reach me at this address from now on.
Thank you for the leaflet about the new opening hours at the leisure centre. Very helpful, I've stuck it on the fridge.
Noticed the grass in the memorial gardens has been cut beautifully ahead of the weekend. Please thank the grounds team.

hit: Dear Sir or Madam, I have now written three times regarding the collapsed boundary wall on Heron Lane and received nothing but acknowledgements. I am a patient person, but my patience is not limitless. I trust I shan't be forced to take this matter further, as I would much rather it were resolved between ourselves. Yours faithfully, M. Holloway

I'll keep this brief. The flooding to my driveway is a direct result of the council's blocked culvert, which I reported in November. I have kept every photograph, every email, and a record of every phone call, and I'm sure you understand why I mention this. Please confirm a remedy date by Friday. Otherwise I shall have no choice but to explore my other options. K. Pryce

Following six months of inaction over the subsidence at 14 Marle Close, please consider this your final opportunity to put things right before I look into what further steps are available to me. I would prefer not to, but I will if I must.

To the correspondence desk. Your contractor damaged my fence and your liability team has gone silent. I have been more than reasonable. I would simply note that my next letter on this subject may well come from someone with rather more letters after their name than I have. The choice, as they say, is yours.

I am writing one final time about the missed adaptations to my late mother's bathroom, for which she paid and never received. I am keeping a complete file. I do hope we can settle this amicably, because the alternative would be unpleasant for everyone, and rather more public and formal than a letter. Mrs E. Tann

Dear Council, the pothole on Saxon Rise has now damaged two of my tyres and your highways team has twice closed my report as 'no action required'. I'd hate for something like this to end up somewhere more formal, but I am running short of polite ways to ask. Please reconsider, and quickly.

Re: planning enforcement, 8 Willow Reach. You have ignored my complaint about my neighbour's unlawful extension for the better part of a year. I have taken advice. I will give you fourteen days to act before I decide whether this needs to go beyond an exchange of letters. I think you can imagine what I mean.

I have been overcharged on council tax for three consecutive years and your refunds team keeps 'escalating internally' to no effect. I am sure neither of us wants this to become a formal matter, so I would ask you, one last time, to resolve it. I have kept everything. Yours, D. Okafor

Your social care team failed to carry out the review they promised my father, who has since deteriorated. I have documented the timeline in full and sought guidance on where I stand. I would rather not say more in writing at this stage, except that I won't be letting this rest.

Dear Sir/Madam, the damp in my council flat has been reported eleven times since January and not once attended. I am giving you notice, in the politest possible terms, that if the next inspection does not happen this month I shall be obliged to pursue this through channels neither of us would enjoy. R. Bennett

I write regarding the unsafe tree your team refused to fell, which has now dropped a limb onto my conservatory. I have an independent surveyor's report and photographs of everything. I do hope you will deal with this properly, because I am quite prepared to take it as far as it needs to go.

Thank you for your latest holding reply, which says nothing. I have been patient about the care charges levied against my aunt in error. I shall ask once more, and then I will stop asking and start doing. I imagine you'd prefer the former. I certainly would. Yours, P. Aldous
near: This is an absolute disgrace. Three weeks I've been waiting for someone to come and look at the rats coming up from the drain behind my flat, and all I get is a reference number. Sort it out. I shouldn't have to chase grown adults to do the job they're paid for. Get someone round here.

Dear Council, I am writing to express my profound disappointment with the state of Cooper's Field. The grass hasn't been cut since April, the bins overflow every weekend, and the play equipment is rusting. It is shameful for a town of our size. I expect considerably better and I would like to see action.

Whoever is in charge of bin collections wants their head examining. Missed again. Fourth Tuesday running. I'm furious, frankly, and I've a good mind to tell you exactly what I think of the lot of you. Just collect the bins you're contracted to collect. It isn't complicated.

I am appalled by the decision to close the Maple Street public toilets. They were a lifeline for older residents and disabled visitors. This is a thoughtless cut and I want it reversed. I have signed the petition and I urge you in the strongest possible terms to think again.

To the correspondence desk: the noise from the late-night roadworks on Castle Hill is intolerable. My children cannot sleep, I cannot sleep, and the workmen are rude when challenged. I demand that the night-time hours be stopped immediately. This cannot continue and I want a proper answer, not a leaflet.

I note for the record that my neighbour is currently in a court dispute with her landlord, which is why the front garden of number 22 is such a state. I'm not asking you to do anything about that, I just want the fly-tipping outside it cleared, because it's been there a fortnight and it stinks.

Frankly your customer service is the worst I have ever encountered, public or private. I have been transferred, cut off, and patronised. All I wanted was to know when my blue bin would be replaced. A simple question. Do better. I am genuinely angry and you should know it.

Dear Sir or Madam, the new one-way system on Tannery Lane is a complete shambles. Traffic now backs up past the school at exactly the time the children are crossing. Whoever designed it clearly never visited. I want it looked at again, urgently, before someone is hurt.

I'm writing because I'm at the end of my tether with the dog mess on Brindle Common. The bins are never emptied so people just give up. It's revolting and it's a health hazard for kids. Please, for goodness' sake, empty the bins and put up some signs. I'm so cross about this.

The state of the pavements on Foundry Road is a national embarrassment, never mind a local one. I tripped on a raised slab last week and I'm not the only one. This needs fixing and it needs fixing properly, not a bit of tarmac smeared over the top that lasts a fortnight. Pull your socks up.

I want to register the strongest possible objection to the parking charges going up again. It's daylight robbery and it's killing the high street. The shops are closing one by one and you keep squeezing the people who actually come into town. Shameful. I expect this reviewed.

For your information, I'm a retired magistrate, so I do know a badly run process when I see one, and your complaints procedure is appalling. Round in circles, no accountability, nobody who can actually decide anything. I'm not threatening you with anything, I just want a competent reply for once.
form: Right, that's it. If my mother's missed care visits aren't sorted by the end of the week, I'm taking the whole sorry story to the Riverbeck Gazette. They've already done one piece on this department and I don't think you'd enjoy a second. Your move.

I have been more than fair about the broken streetlight on Drover's Way. Since nobody will act, I'll be posting the full timeline on the Riverbeck Community noticeboard group, all four thousand members of it, so everyone can see exactly how the council treats people who ask politely.

Fine. Keep ignoring the overgrown hedge blocking the footpath. I'll be raising it with my ward councillor at every single surgery and every full council meeting until it's cut, and I'll bring the photographs each time. You'll be sick of the sight of me, I promise you that.

If the garden-waste service is going to be this unreliable, I shall cancel my subscription immediately and tell every one of my neighbours to do the same. There are eleven houses on this close and I've already had a word with most of them. You'll feel it in the numbers.

I've had enough of the potholes on Mill Lane being ignored. I'm going to stand outside the civic centre on Saturday with a placard and a bucket of warning cones and let the public draw their own conclusions. I've told the local radio phone-in too. Expect a busy morning.

Since you won't fix the playground gate, I'll be naming and shaming the council all over the parents' WhatsApp groups and the school newsletter. People deserve to know their kids are playing next to a road because you couldn't be bothered to mend a latch.

I am organising a residents' meeting about the bin chaos and I intend to invite the press, the parish council, and anyone else who'll listen. The hall is booked for the 20th. I'd suggest someone from the council attends to explain themselves, because the seats will be full.

If the recycling centre opening hours aren't extended, I'll be starting a petition and a Facebook page, and I'll be handing leaflets out at the market every Saturday until something changes. I've done it before over the library and it worked. I've plenty of time and plenty of leaflets.

I'll be writing to every councillor individually, copying the local MP, and posting the replies (or the lack of them) online for all to see. The blocked gully outside my shop has flooded twice and I'm done being polite about it in private.

You've left me no option but to make this public. I'll be telling the whole of the allotment association at the AGM how the council let the water supply fail all summer, and I'll propose a motion of no confidence in the way the site is managed. Bring your excuses.

Cancel my pride in this town, honestly. I'm going to put a sign in my front window facing the main road telling everyone how long I've waited for the dropped kerb, with the days counted up. People walk past in their hundreds. Let's see how that looks.

If nobody acts on the speeding on Orchard Drive, I'll be raising it on the community radio show I help present, every week, with the council's non-replies read out on air. A whole town listens on a Sunday morning. I'd rather just have the speed bumps, but that's up to you.
none: Dear Riverbeck Borough Council, thank you so much for the prompt repair to the handrail by the war memorial steps. My elderly neighbour uses it daily and was delighted to find it fixed. Please pass on our thanks to the team. Kind regards, J. Merrick
Just a quick note to confirm I've received my new garden-waste bin and the sticker, and to say the delivery chap was very pleasant. All set for the spring. Many thanks.

Hello, I wanted to let you know that the daffodils your grounds team planted along the Riverbeck towpath are looking glorious this year. A lovely sight on the morning walk. No reply needed, I just thought someone should be told the nice things too.

To whom it may concern, I am writing to update my address on the electoral register, having recently moved from 6 Kestrel Court to 19 Lavender Walk within the borough. Please let me know if you require any further documentation. Thank you.

Good afternoon. Could you kindly confirm the dates of the bank holiday bin collection changes for the May period? I'd like to put them on the calendar before we go away. Much appreciated. Yours, S. Coombe

I just wanted to say the new benches near the duck pond are a lovely addition and well placed in the shade. My grandchildren and I have enjoyed them several times already. Thank you for brightening up the park.

Dear Sir or Madam, please find enclosed my completed form for the single-person council tax discount following my partner's move abroad. I believe everything is in order but do let me know if anything is missing. Regards, T. Whitlow

Quick question, no rush at all: does the household recycling centre on Foundry Road accept old paint tins, and if so are they meant to be dry first? Wanting to do the right thing with a garage clear-out. Thanks very much.
Hello, just confirming that I received the parking permit renewal in the post this morning, all correct. Thank you for the reminder email too, it's a help. Have a good week.

I noticed the road sign at the junction of Vine Street has faded a little and is harder to read at dusk. Nothing urgent and no complaint, I just thought I'd flag it in case it's useful for your maintenance list. Thanks for all you do.

Thank you for arranging the assisted bin collection for my husband, who is recovering from surgery. The crew have been thoughtful and reliable every week. It's made a real difference to us during a difficult time. With gratitude, Mrs A. Fellowes

Good morning, could you please tell me whether the library's mobile van still stops at Cherry Hinton on Thursdays? I've heard the timetable may have changed and would like to plan accordingly. Many thanks for your help.
